The Fear of Hadhrat Khabbaab bin Arat (RA) and his Weeping Over Worldly Prosperity
The Incident when some Sahabah (RA) Visited him

Hadhrat Yahya bin Ja'dah reports that some Sahabah (RA) once visited Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) during his illness. They said, "Good news for you, O Abu Abdullaah! You shall meet Muhammad ﷺ at the pond." He then pointed to the top and bottom storeys of his house and said, "How is that possible with all this when Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'All that one of you requires are the provisions of a traveller'?"[^2]
The Incident when he Passed Away

Hadhrat Taariq bin Shihaab reports that a group of Sahabah (RA) once visited Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) during his illness and said, "Good news for you, O Abu Abdullaah! You shall be meeting your brothers tomorrow." Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) then started weeping saying, "Remember that I am not afraid (of death). However, (I am crying because) you have reminded me of a group of people and called them my brothers whereas they have passed on with all their rewards intact (all reserved for the Aakhirah without receiving any part of it in this world). What I fear is that we may have already been given the rewards for the deeds you have mentioned (in this world) since we have lived on after them (and received much wealth)."[^3]

Hadhrat Haaritha bin Mudarrib reports that when they visited Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA), he had already taken seven brandings with a hot iron on his stomach (as treatment for his illness). He said, "Had Rasulullaah ﷺ not stated that no person should ever wish for death, I would have certainly wished for it now." Someone said to him, "(Why worry about your future?) Rather call to mind your companionship with Rasulullaah ﷺ and that you will soon be going to him." Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) responded by saying, "I fear that what I have with me, may prevent me from meeting with him. I have forty thousand Dirhams here in my house."[^4]

Another similar narration adds that Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) said, "I saw a time when I was with Rasulullaah ﷺ without a single Dirham to my name. I now have beside my room forty thousand Dirhams."
